article.title: Comas
article.part: Participios y deeprichastiya — Причастия и деепричастия

claims.summary: Introduces the concept of a 'деепричастный оборот' (gerundive construction) in Russian, stating it is formed by a participle and its complements and is normally separated by commas from the rest of the sentence.

Explains the punctuation rules for the gerundive construction depending on its position in the sentence, and clarifies that the comma marks the relative syntactic independence of the secondary action but does not determine its temporal interpretation.
Provides several examples of the gerundive construction in Russian sentences, demonstrating its usage in different contexts.

Notes that while the general rule is to separate the gerundive construction with commas, there are some fixed expressions and lexicalized forms that may behave differently. It advises distinguishing between a living verbal construction and a lexicalized unit.
